decided: AMENDS the earlier workspace-dfd decision on this branch, on three points, after a false premise was corrected and pre-PR review confirmed four findings. (1) CORRECTED PREMISE: golangci-lint is NOT absent from this machine. It is installed at $(go env GOBIN)/golangci-lint and merely off PATH — but at version 2.13.2, while CI pins 2.13.1. So the real hazard was never 'command not found'; it was that the obvious fix, running whatever binary the machine has, would have made the local gate run a DIFFERENT analyzer version from CI — a quieter instance of exactly the drift this bead exists to close. The resolution order therefore searches PATH, then $GOBIN, then $GOPATH/bin, and accepts a candidate ONLY if `version --short` equals the pin; anything else falls back to `go run` at the pin. Observed on this machine: 'ignoring golangci-lint not at the pinned 2.13.1: /Users/yauvansuba/go/bin/golangci-lint (2.13.2)'. (2) The gate job is now in scope. The `warden gate` job runs `warden verify --scope core`, and its base-ref pin list covers .warden/bin, .warden/rules, .warden/skills-policy.md, repo.yaml and graph.yaml but NOT scripts/. Once a six-step verify.core is on main, that job reaches `ci-go.sh lint` on a runner with no linter and takes the from-source `go run` path — the network-fragile build this repo already rejected, silently acquired by a second required check. The checksum-verified install is extracted to scripts/install-golangci-lint.sh and called by BOTH the core job and the gate job (in the gate job before the base-ref pin, so it does not depend on a base ref that predates the script and runs before the deploy key is on disk). (3) `lint` now runs with an explicit config: this repo's .golangci.* if one exists, otherwise --no-config. golangci-lint searches every ancestor directory and $HOME for a config, so an unrelated .golangci.yml above someone's clone silently changed which linters ran locally while CI's bare runner had none — a fail-open parity hole in the exact mechanism this bead is about. Also narrowed, per review: the parity claim is over the six CHECKS, not over the job's verdict, since the job additionally installs the linter.
why: Three corrections, each forced by evidence rather than preference. On (1): the founder-side premise that the linter was missing was wrong, and the tempting simplification it invited — resolve $GOPATH/bin and be done — is wrong for a reason the wrong premise hid. A 2.13.2 binary standing in for a 2.13.1 pin reproduces this bead's own defect one level down: two gates, same name, different analysis. Preferring an installed binary ONLY at the pin keeps the fast path available (CI's checksum-verified install hits it; so does a developer who installs the pinned version) while making the pin, not the machine, decide the analyzer version. On (2): the cross-examiner verified every link — the gate job does run verify --scope core, scripts/ is genuinely absent from its base-ref pin list, no golangci-lint exists on that runner, and the effect starts on the first PR after this merges. Leaving it would have meant this PR fixing a parity gap in one required job while opening a flake in another, and the first decision record's scope section never mentioned that job at all. On (3): the config search was verified empirically against the pinned binary's own source and by demonstration — a stray ancestor config turned a real ineffassign finding into 'no linters enabled', and --no-config restored it. A gate whose linter set depends on directories above the repo is not the same gate in two places, which is the one property this whole item is buying.
cost_if_wrong: Each amendment is separately reversible and none weakens a check. (1) The candidate search adds two stat-and-exec probes per lint run; if a machine has a slow or hanging golangci-lint on PATH the probe inherits that, bounded by one `version --short` call, and a failed probe falls through to the pin rather than failing the run. Worst case is the status quo ante: `go run` at the pin, measured at ~20-37s across 18 modules. (2) The extracted installer is a new file under scripts/, HIGH tier: a bug there fails CI loudly (it exits 2 on an unknown version, a non-linux-amd64 host, or a post-install version mismatch, and sha256sum -c gates the binary), and it can only ever install the exact checksummed tarball. Running it in the gate job before the base-ref pin means it is PR-controlled code on a runner — but that runner already executes the PR's own scripts/ci-go.sh through warden verify, and this step runs before the deploy key is written, so it adds no capability that job did not have. (3) --no-config is the strictest option and is exactly what CI's bare runner already effectively had; the day this repo adopts a .golangci.yml, the script picks it up by path and both sides read the same file. If any of this proves wrong, the whole amendment reverts to the previous commit without touching the six-step verify.core that is the item's actual deliverable.
alternatives: Resolve $(go env GOPATH)/bin unconditionally and use whatever golangci-lint is there — REJECTED after checking the version: the installed binary is 2.13.2 and CI pins 2.13.1, so this would have shipped a local gate that runs a different analyzer from the required job. That is the same defect class as the step-list drift, only harder to see, and it would have been introduced by the change meant to fix it.

Bump the pin to 2.13.2 to match the machine — REJECTED: the checksum on record is 2.13.1's, and a pin bump is a deliberate act with its own checksum update, not a side effect of one machine's `go install`. The gate should not follow whatever a developer happens to have.

Leave the gate job alone and note the from-source build in a comment — REJECTED: it converts a confirmed defect into documentation of a defect, in a REQUIRED check, and the flake evidence against that build path is this repo's own.

Duplicate the curl+sha256 install block inline in the gate job — REJECTED: two hardcoded copies of one checksum is a second home for the pin, which is the shape of the bug this item exists to remove. One script, called twice.

Add scripts/ to the gate job's base-ref pin list (it is declared gate surface and HIGH tier, and the step's comment says it restores 'the entire executable gate surface') — NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: it is a real pre-existing hole but a separate change with its own bootstrap-ordering consequences, and folding it into this PR would mean a gate-surface edit no finding asked for. Filed as a follow-up item instead.

Ship a .golangci.yml so the linter set is pinned by a file rather than by --no-config — REJECTED again, same reason as the first record: choosing the linter SET is a different decision from making both sides run the same one. --no-config makes local match CI's actual behaviour today, and the script already prefers a repo config the moment one lands.
scope: Unchanged from the first record except as stated: adds scripts/install-golangci-lint.sh (new), adds an install step to ci.yml's gate job, adds config pinning and the GOBIN/GOPATH candidate search to scripts/ci-go.sh, and narrows the parity wording in repo.yaml, .warden/skills-policy.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and .github/pull_request_template.md. Still no Go source, no library behaviour change, and nothing under adapters/export/gcp/, docs/adapters.md, README.md or docs/architecture/, which other agents hold concurrently. workspace-dfd remains the tracked item that .warden/skills-policy.md's Forbidden paths section requires for a gate-surface PR.
